key_insight: VLA-JEPA introduces leakage-free state prediction in a JEPA-style pretraining framework so the model learns action-relevant latent dynamics instead of low-level pixel variation.
problem_solved: Existing latent-action objectives latch onto pixel changes and nuisance motion (appearance bias and information leakage), producing representations that do not reliably capture true action/state transitions for vision-language-action policies.
method: Use a JEPA-style pretraining objective where a predictor forecasts target latent states rather than raw pixels, removing shortcuts to appearance cues.
Design a target encoder and training constraints (bottleneck/stop-gradient/architectural choices) that prevent pixel-level information leakage into the predicted latent.
Train a latent world model on large-scale video to capture action-relevant transitions, integrating vision-language-action inputs for downstream policy learning.
impact: Produces more robust, generalizable VLA policies that are less sensitive to appearance changes and nuisance motions—improving downstream action prediction, imitation, and control from video-scale pretraining.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input video + language → encoder → latent world model predictor → leakage-free target encoder (show stop-gradient/bottleneck icon).
Before/After comparison: two panels showing pixel-anchored representations failing under appearance change vs. leakage-free latents preserving action semantics.
Latent-space visualization: t-SNE or UMAP showing clustered action states learned by VLA-JEPA versus dispersed pixel-driven features.
Bar chart or robustness plot: metrics (e.g., generalization accuracy, sensitivity to appearance/nuisance motion) comparing baseline latent-action methods to VLA-JEPA.
paper_title: VLA-JEPA: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Model with Latent World Model
paper_authors: Jingwen Sun, Wenyao Zhang, Zekun Qi, Shaojie Ren, Zezhi Liu
